messages:
maria: Heads-up — we're seeing a sudden spike of 401s from hosted API clients starting ~09:02 UTC. Errors across eu-west and us-central. Error from auth-proxy: "introspection: jwks fetch failed (404)".
kevin: looking... are we seeing any recent JWKS publishes or key rotations?
eli: i see a successful key-publish event at 08:59 from key-service, but subsequent introspect calls started getting 404 when fetching /jwks.json from the key store.
sara: this matches incoming support tickets — customers report 'invalid_api_key' and token introspection failing.
julian: deploy-bot just reported a key-service deployment at 08:58 (canary). Deploy ID: deploy-20240312-1147. Could be related.
oncall-bot: alert: auth.introspection.error_rate > 5% for 3m in eu-west. Pager duty triggered.
maria: ops note: curl from within vpc to https://keystore.internal/jwks.json returns 404. But the object list on s3 shows keys/active/{kid}.json present.
kevin: weird — path mismatch? Key-service should serve /jwks.json aggregated. Check the aggregator lambda/logs.
eli: tailing key-agg logs: ERROR "failed to write jwks file: file missing for kid=K-2024-03-12-1". Then aggregator returned 200 with an empty body.
sara: so introspect clients saw a 200 but no jwks? our auth clients fall back to error. Some return 401 explicitly when JWKS can't be parsed.
maria: immediate mitigation: can we point auth-proxy to cached jwks endpoint -> auth-proxy config has fallback_jwks_url.
kevin: switching fallback in auth-proxy now to https://s3-cache.internal/jwks/latest — patching config in staging then rolling to prod.
eli: command i used to test: 
```
curl -v https://auth-proxy.internal/introspect -d 'token=xxx'
# response: HTTP/1.1 401
# body: {"error":"jwks_not_found"}
```
maria: rolling the config in prod to use s3-cache fallback. doing canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%.
deploy-bot: Rollout started: auth-proxy/config/fallback -> s3-cache (canary 10%) (id: r-8841).
julian: while rolling, i pushed a re-publish job to key-service to re-generate aggregated jwks.json from individual kid files. kicked off manually.
sara: support update: please post a short blurb for customers: "We are investigating intermittent 401s for token validation. Temporary mitigation applied, engineering investigating root cause."
kevin: quick root cause hypothesis: the key-agg job has a TTL pruning step that removes keys older than X days. There was a timezone bug in prune which treated today's new key as older and removed it from the aggregated file during the canary deploy. That would explain the missing kid in the jwks manifest.
eli: confirm: prune job logs: "removed kid=K-2024-03-12-1 reason=expired ts=2024-03-11T23:59:59Z" — prune used localtime vs UTC boundary. The new key got flagged.
maria: oof. so the aggregator then tried to rebuild jwks.json but saw missing kid and wrote an empty file then returned 200.
kevin: mitigation complete: auth-proxy fallback rollout at 100% and key-agg re-publish completed. jwks.json now contains expected keys. introspection success rate back to normal.
oncall-bot: alert cleared: auth.introspection.error_rate dropped below threshold.
eli: next steps: revert the pruning change in key-service, add a safety check in aggregator to never publish empty jwks.json, and add an alert if jwks.json size < 1KB.
sara: I'll draft the customer status update and API status page blurb.
maria: creating incident ticket INC-2024-314 in tracker and assigning RCAs: kevin for code fix, eli for tests/monitoring, julian for deploy safeguards.
kevin: proposed code fix: in prune_job, compare timestamps in UTC and require min_age > 24h plus a grace_window of 2h for new keys. Also add unit test for daylight saving/timezone edge.
eli: plus aggregator patch: atomic write -> write to temp file then mv to jwks.json to avoid empty publishes, and if any kid missing, fail publish and keep previous file.
julian: adding deploy guard: block key-service prune deploys from running during active canaries and require a manual verification step.
maria: support posts sent, customers notified. Monitoring ticket created to track regressions.
sara: note for postmortem: impact window 09:02-09:12 UTC, ~10% of tokens introspection failed in eu-west and us-central, customer-facing API 401s for ~1200 requests.
maria: thanks all. we'll keep this thread updated with the RCA and timeline. :white_check_mark:
